subject: science
source: NCERT Our Wondrous World (Class V), Chapter 2

levelNotes.easy: Facts from the chapter – who, what, where.
levelNotes.hard: Why and how questions – use what you learnt.
levelNotes.advanced: Think like a scientist: real-life puzzles and tricky reasoning, still from this chapter.

questions.q: Where does the river Godavari begin its journey?
questions.a: Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats, Maharashtra
questions.e: It starts as a stream in the Brahmagiri Hills of the Western Ghats.

questions.q: How long is the Godavari?
questions.e: It travels 1,465 km before joining the Bay of Bengal.

questions.q: The Godavari joins the…
questions.e: It flows east across India.

questions.q: The Godavari is the second longest river in India after the…
questions.e: It is also called Dakshina Ganga.

questions.q: Small streams that join a river are called its…
questions.e: Indravati, Manjira and Sabari are tributaries of the Godavari.

questions.q: A river that flows all year round is called a…
questions.e: Seasonal rivers flow only in the rainy season.

questions.q: What forms where the Godavari reaches the sea and spreads into many small streams?
questions.e: Its freshwater meets the salty sea at the Coringa mangrove forests.

questions.q: Why is the Godavari called ‘Dakshina Ganga’?
questions.a: It flows through southern India and is regarded as sacred
w: It is longer than the Ganga
questions.e: Dakshina means south.

questions.q: Which of these is true about “{x}” in the Godavari’s journey?
questions.e: {x} → {ans}.

questions.q: Which of these is true about “{x}” in the Godavari’s journey?
questions.e: {x} → {ans}.

questions.q: Since ancient times, people built homes near rivers because…
questions.a: rivers give water for drinking, farming and work
questions.e: Rivers provide water for drinking, cooking, washing, crops and factories.

questions.q: A dam stores river water in a large water body called a…
questions.e: A dam is like a giant wall that blocks the river’s flow.

questions.q: About how many dams store the Godavari’s water?
questions.e: They help people use water even in dry seasons.

questions.q: Which is a problem caused when a dam is built?
questions.a: Land that was home to people and animals gets flooded
w: There is more water in the dry season
questions.e: Many people have to leave their homes and shift elsewhere.

questions.q: Ecotourism means…
questions.a: visiting natural places to enjoy and learn without harming the environment
questions.e: Watching animals and birds in forests, rivers or mountains carefully.

questions.q: Which of these pollutes a river?
questions.e: Waste from people and factories makes river water unsafe.

questions.q: In Activity 3, sugar and cooking oil are stirred in water. What happens?
questions.e: Some things dissolve in water and some do not – harmful things can hide in clear-looking water.

questions.q: What causes a ‘green blanket’ on a river?
questions.a: Fertilisers washed from fields make plants grow very fast
questions.e: The green layer chokes life; fish find it hard to breathe.

questions.q: Even when river water looks clean it may be unsafe because…
questions.a: harmful chemicals or soapy water can be dissolved in it
questions.e: Things that dissolve cannot be seen.

questions.q: Which programme helps clean the river Ganga?
questions.e: It keeps the Ganga healthy for people, fish and birds.

questions.q: Does {x} dissolve in water?
questions.e: {x}: {ans}.

questions.q: Does {x} dissolve in water?
questions.e: {x}: {ans}.

questions.q: When too much rain falls, a river may…
questions.a: overflow its banks and flood the land
questions.e: Flood water damages houses, fields and roads.

questions.q: How do trees help reduce flooding?
questions.a: They slow down rainwater and help the soil soak it up
w: They drink all the river water
questions.e: Without trees, water runs off faster and causes floods.

questions.q: Which is a flood safety tip?
w: Go home before it is declared safe
questions.e: Also keep an emergency bag with food, medicines and a flashlight.

questions.q: In 2019, which city had to bring water by special trains because its reservoirs dried up?
questions.e: In 2022, heavy rains flooded Bengaluru – too little and too much water both cause problems.

questions.q: Which is a good way to save water?
questions.a: Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth
w: Throw away water after washing vegetables
Use drinking water to wash the car
questions.e: Every drop counts!

questions.q: Water left from washing fruits and vegetables can be…
questions.e: Reusing clean water is a small step that helps.

questions.q: True or false? Water ATMs give clean water when you put in a card or coin.
questions.e: They help people get safe water and use it wisely.

questions.q: The Godavari is 1,465 km long. A boat travels {s} km along it each day. About how many whole days would it take to cover the river?
questions.e: 1,465 ÷ {s} ≈ {ans} days (rounding up so the last part is covered).

questions.q: A new dam will give water to a city but flood a forest village. What is the fairest plan?
questions.a: Build it only after the villagers are safely moved and given new homes and land
w: Build it and ignore the villagers
questions.e: Dams help many people, but those who lose homes must be taken care of.

questions.q: A town throws soapy water into the river and farms use lots of fertiliser. Which result is most likely?
questions.a: A green blanket forms, fish struggle to breathe and the water becomes unsafe
w: The water turns salty like the sea
questions.e: Fertilisers make plants grow fast; soap and chemicals dissolve and harm life.

questions.q: Flood problem → what it affects: which pair is correct?
questions.e: Dirty water → safe drinking; broken roads → travel; lost crops → food supply; no electricity → lights and fans.

questions.q: You are planning a new city near a river. Which set of steps helps with BOTH floods and water shortage?
questions.a: Plant trees, keep open land and collect rainwater
w: Build homes on the river bank
questions.e: Trees and open land reduce floods and recharge groundwater; rainwater harvesting stores water for dry days.

questions.q: What is the difference between a perennial and a seasonal river?
questions.a: A perennial river flows all year; a seasonal river flows only in the rainy season
questions.e: The Godavari is perennial.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT found in the forests along the Godavari?
questions.e: The book mentions tigers, barking deer, the Indian golden gecko and red sandalwood.

questions.q: How does river water reach houses, schools and fields far away?
questions.e: The river’s water is carried in pipes and canals and shared by many.

questions.q: Why should we never waste tap water?
questions.a: Its journey from the river needed dams, pipes and sacrifices by people who lost their homes
questions.e: It is hard to imagine the journey water has taken to reach our taps.
